title: Climate Regions of the World
summary: The main world climate regions, their temperature, rainfall and natural vegetation, how people live in them, and the climate regions of South Africa.

notes.text: A **climate region** is a large area with a similar pattern of temperature and rainfall. Similar climates produce similar natural vegetation (**biomes**), so the vegetation of a region often reflects its climate.

notes.caption: Main world climate regions
rows: Near the equator: Congo Basin, Amazon
Hot all year (about 27 °C); heavy rain every month (over 2 000 mm)
Dense, tall evergreen forest with layers
Between the rainforests and deserts: much of southern and East Africa
Grassland with scattered trees (e.g. acacia, baobab)
Around the tropics: Sahara, Namib, Kalahari
Very hot days, cold nights; less than 250 mm rain a year
Very little; plants adapted to store water (succulents)
West coasts at about 30° to 40°: Western Cape, California, Mediterranean Sea
Hot, dry summers; mild, wet winters
Interiors of continents: Highveld, prairies of North America
Warm summers with rain; cold, dry winters with frost
Mild all year; rain in all seasons
Mosses, lichens, small shrubs; ice sheets

notes.title: Living in a hot desert
notes.problem: How have people adapted to life in hot deserts, such as the Kalahari?
steps: Clothing: loose, light-coloured clothes covering the body to protect against the sun and keep cool.
Water: people traditionally knew where to find water in roots, melons and underground sources; today boreholes are used.
Movement: traditional San hunter-gatherers and pastoralists moved with the seasons to find food and water.
Housing: thick walls or temporary shelters that keep out the heat.
notes.answer: People adapt clothing, water use, movement and housing to the extreme heat and dryness.

items: In the **tropical rainforest**, people practise shifting cultivation; today logging, mining and farming destroy the forest.
In the **savanna**, many people keep cattle and grow crops in the wet season; it is also home to large game reserves.
The **Mediterranean** climate is ideal for growing grapes, citrus and wheat, as in the Western Cape.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: When describing a climate graph, always mention the **temperature** (hot or cold; the range), the **total rainfall**, and **when** the rain falls (summer, winter or all year). Then name the climate region.

questions.prompt: Which climate region is hot and wet all year?
Hot deserts receive less than how many millimetres of rain a year?
What is the natural vegetation of the Mediterranean climate region in the Western Cape?

options: rain all year and no frost

questions.prompt: Savanna vegetation is grassland with scattered trees.
Match each place to its climate region.
A climate graph shows temperatures of 20–28 °C all year, rain mainly from November to March, and a dry winter. Name the climate region and explain your answer.
questions.memo:
✓ Tropical savanna (1)
✓ Hot all year (1)
✓ Summer rainfall with a dry winter season (1)

questions.prompt: Describe THREE ways people adapt to living in a hot desert.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): loose, light clothing; covering head/body from sun; finding/storing water; boreholes; moving with seasons; thick-walled houses

questions.prompt: Why is the Western Cape suitable for growing grapes?
questions.memo:
✓ It has a Mediterranean climate (1)
✓ Hot, dry summers ripen the grapes, and winter rain provides water (1)
